UAV Competition

About the Competition

The UAV Competition is a team-based technical event focused on UAV design, flight control, mission execution, safety, and technical understanding. Teams will operate their UAVs in a designated offline flight area and complete the assigned mission while following all safety requirements.

Eligibility

  • Open to students currently pursuing any degree program.

  • Participants may belong to any college or university.

  • Each team must consist of 3–6 members.

  • All team members must satisfy the eligibility requirements.

  • A safety briefing is mandatory before the flight activity.

  • There is no registration fee.

Team Size

Minimum: 3 members
Maximum: 6 members

Format

The competition will be conducted as a direct offline final event.

The event will consist of the following activities:

1. Technical & Safety Inspection

  • All UAVs will undergo a mandatory technical and safety inspection before flight.

  • The UAV must be airworthy and comply with the safety requirements specified by the organizers.

  • The organizing team may inspect the UAV, batteries, propulsion system, control system, and other relevant components.

  • Only UAVs that successfully pass the inspection will be permitted to fly.

2. Mission Flight

  • Teams will complete the assigned mission using their UAV.

  • Mission tasks may include activities such as payload drop, navigation, mapping, target identification, or other tasks announced by the organizers.

  • Teams must complete the assigned task within the specified time limit.

  • All flights must take place within the designated flight zone.

3. Documentation & Viva

  • Teams may be required to submit a brief design/technical report.

  • The judging panel may ask questions regarding the UAV's design, components, control system, flight operation, and mission strategy.

  • Team members should be able to explain their respective technical contributions.

Rules & Regulations

  1. All UAVs must pass the mandatory safety inspection before being allowed to fly.

  2. The maximum takeoff weight and permitted flight altitude will be specified during the venue-specific briefing and must be strictly followed.

  3. Flights are permitted only within the designated flight zone.

  4. Flying over spectators, organizers, restricted areas, or other prohibited zones is strictly forbidden.

  5. At least one team member must have appropriate UAV piloting training or prior flight experience, subject to verification by the organizers.

  6. A mandatory safety briefing must be attended by the participating team before the flight activity.

  7. Teams must follow all instructions given by safety marshals, technical officials, and organizers.

  8. In case of a crash, malfunction, loss of control, or other safety issue, the flight must be stopped immediately and the safety marshals must be informed.

  9. Teams are responsible for bringing their own required batteries, propellers, tools, and other necessary backup equipment. Spare batteries and propellers will not be provided by the organizers.

  10. Any modification made to the UAV after the safety inspection must be approved by the organizers before the UAV is flown again.

  11. Teams must not operate a UAV in a manner that intentionally or negligently endangers people, property, or other participants.

  12. Participants must comply with all applicable safety instructions and venue restrictions communicated by the organizers.

  13. The organizing committee reserves the right to stop or cancel a flight if it considers the operation unsafe.

Equipment & Preparation

  • Teams must bring their own UAV and all equipment required for operation.

  • Teams should carry sufficient batteries and necessary spare components.

  • All equipment must be in safe operating condition.

  • Teams should arrive with adequate time for registration, technical inspection, and the mandatory safety briefing.

  • Any specific technical specifications or equipment restrictions will be communicated before the competition.

Judging Criteria

Teams will be evaluated on:

  • Mission Task Completion

  • Flight Stability & Control

  • Adherence to Safety Protocols

  • Quality of UAV Design

  • Technical Understanding

  • Quality of Documentation

  • Viva / Technical Explanation

  • Overall Performance

Grounds for Disqualification

A team may be disqualified for:

  • Failing the mandatory safety inspection.

  • Flying outside the designated flight zone.

  • Violating specified altitude or weight restrictions.

  • Endangering spectators, organizers, participants, or property.

  • Unauthorized modification of the UAV after inspection.

  • Ignoring instructions from safety marshals or organizers.

  • Deliberately violating safety protocols.

  • Providing false information regarding team members or pilot experience.

  • Tampering with another team's equipment.

  • Serious misconduct or disruptive behavior.

  • Any other action that compromises the safety or fairness of the competition.

Safety & Conduct

  1. Safety takes priority over competition performance.

  2. All participants must behave professionally and responsibly.

  3. Teams must follow instructions from organizers, judges, technical officials, and safety marshals.

  4. Participants must not interfere with another team's UAV or equipment.

  5. Any unsafe operation may result in immediate termination of the flight.

  6. The organizing committee reserves the right to modify, postpone, stop, or cancel a flight for safety reasons.

Results & Judging

  • The judging panel will evaluate teams according to the announced criteria.

  • In case of a tie, the organizers may conduct an additional evaluation or use a predetermined tie-breaker.

  • The judges' decision will be final and binding, subject to correction of any administrative or calculation error.

Registration

Registration Fee: Free
Participation: Students currently pursuing any degree
Team Size: 3–6 Members
Format: Direct Offline Final Competition
Category: Technology / UAV
